articles.headline: USMNT schedule 2026: USA men's soccer games, dates, times, live stream and TV channel including home World Cup
keyFacts: The United States men's national soccer team will co-host the 2026 FIFA World Cup alongside Canada and Mexico in June and July.
The USMNT was drawn into Group D alongside Australia, Paraguay, and a to-be-determined UEFA playoff qualifier.
Following the World Cup, the remainder of the 2026 schedule remains unclear, though the CONCACAF Nations League is expected to resume in the fall.
body: JUMP TO:
As the calendar turns to 2026, the United States men's national soccer team will embark on one of the most significant 12-month period of its entire history.

Set to host the 2026 FIFA World Cup in June and July, the USMNT are hoping to put their best foot forward with the opportunity to captivate the nation and generate unprecedented levels of excitement around the sport of soccer, reaching potential heights this nation has never experienced before.

Success at the World Cup, in the form of a potential run to the quarterfinals or beyond, would position the U.S. to build on that electricity and buzz over the next decade or more. In contrast, disappointment at this summer's tournament could codify the sport's inferior comparative level, squandering a once-in-a-lifetime chance to generate course-altering levels of attention.
While 2026 will be defined by the World Cup, the soccer slate across the calendar year extends across much more than just those two months.
The Sporting News brings you a look at how the USMNT schedule will shape up across 2026 and what is in store for this era-defining year of football across America.

There was no January camp in 2026, as U.S. Soccer has done away with the annual tradition and moved it to December. The United States played two friendlies in the March international break, and then two more in the immediate run-up to the FIFA World Cup.

Then, the focus turns entirely to the 2026 World Cup, with the U.S. playing its first game against Paraguay on Friday, June 12. Their group-stage opponents were determined at the World Cup draw held on December 5.

After the World Cup is complete, it's not known what will fill out the rest of the 2026 schedule. It's believed that the 2025/26 CONCACAF Nations League will begin at some point during the fall, but when is not terribly clear at this stage. There is no precedent for the current post-World Cup calendar in the Nations League era, as the only other time the Nations League was scheduled around a World Cup was in 2022 when the FIFA tournament was contested in December.

It was heavily reported through the fall of 2025 that the USMNT would take on Portugal and Belgium in the March international break, and that was confirmed just prior to the World Cup draw.

U.S. Soccer was forced to wait for Portugal and Belgium to officially secure qualification to the World Cup in the November international break before confirming the matches, ensuring they were free in the March window and not beholden to qualifying playoff obligations that would otherwise have seen them booked if they had failed to see out direct passage.

In a break from usual norms, the U.S. is expected to play both games at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Traditionally, the U.S. national team travels to play matches in different locations throughout individual international breaks. This time, they would play both matches in the same location.
Those games were eventually confirmed, and the U.S. were beaten in both by multiple goals, stoking fears of a World Cup disappointment.
USMNT pre-World Cup schedule

According to a report by The Athletic in the fall of 2025 and confirmed in December, the United States had lined up a pair of friendlies in the run-up to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, to be played in late May and early June right before the start of the tournament.

It is commonplace for most World Cup participants to play one or two friendlies just prior to the start of the competition to work out any last-minute kinks and get players into game shape with the national team.

The first match of the pre-World Cup camp was played against Senegal in Charlotte, NC at Bank of America Stadium while the final send-off game took place in Chicago. The second opponent will be Germany, with the game at Soldier Field.

The selection to play Senegal before the start of the tournament was somewhat odd. It is common for World Cup preparations to include games against teams with similar style to that of the opponents a given country is set to face at the competition itself, yet there were no African teams drawn alongside the U.S. in the World Cup group stage.

During this time, the home base for the U.S. national team will be their new facility in Fayetteville, Gerogia. They will then set up World Cup camp in Southern California for the tournament itself, given that most of their matches are likely to take place on the west coast.
The United States will take part in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, playing host to the famed competition for the second time following the 1994 tournament won by Brazil.
This time, they are joint-hosts alongside Canada and Mexico, as the tournament is played across nations for just the second time ever after the 2002 competition in South Korea and Japan.
USMNT in the group stage of the 2026 FIFA World Cup
As hosts of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the United States have been pre-drawn out of Pot 1 into Group D.

They have been drawn alongside Australia (FIFA #26) from Pot 2, Paraguay (FIFA #39) from Pot 3, and a to-be-determined UEFA playoff qualifier from Pot 4, from which either Slovakia, Kosovo, Turkey, or Romania will join the group.
It's an extremely soft and kind draw for the 2026 co-hosts, who secure two of the lower-ranked sides from Pot 2 and 3, and grab arguably the easiest of the four UEFA pathways from Pot 4.
USMNT group stage fixtures
Group D standings
USMNT in the knockout stage of the 2026 FIFA World Cup

While the group-stage slate for the USMNT was already solidified well in advance of the tournament, their potential knockout pathway remains up in the air until they secure mathematical qualification.
Should the U.S. qualify for the Round of 32, either by placing top two in their group or being one of the eight third-place qualifiers, they have five potential places they could end up in.
Here are all five possible locations the U.S. could wind up slotting into, as well as their path to the final from each one.
Path for USA in World Cup knockout — 1st place in Group D
Path for USA in World Cup knockout — 2nd place in Group D
Path for USA in World Cup knockout — 3rd place qualifier
As a member of Group D, the United States have three potential places in the knockout stage bracket they could be sorted into should they qualify as one of the eight third-place qualifiers.

Until all qualifiers are known, it is impossible to predict where or when they could potentially play should this come to pass. There are 495 mathematical combinations of third place qualifiers, with 330 of them involving a participant from Group D. All of these have been spelled out in advance, and every potential outcome can be found in Annex C (pg. 80) of the 2026 FIFA World Cup regulations.
Potential path 1 — Face Winner of Group E
There are 202 total combinations of third-place qualifiers that would see the U.S. play the winner from Group E, which is by far the most likely result.
Potential path 2 — Face Winner of Group I
There are 111 possible combinations of third-place qualifiers that would see the USMNT face the winner of Group I in the Round of 32.
Potential path 3 — Face Winner of Group K

This is by far the least likely scenario for if the U.S. were to qualify as a third place finisher, with only 17 of the possible 495 combinations of third-place qualifiers resulting in this placement.
* If USA qualifies via 1st place in Group D
** If USA qualifies via 2nd place in Group D
It's likely that the fall of 2026 will see the resumption of the CONCACAF Nations League for the 2026/27 edition of the competition.
The annual tournament, which was created to cut down on the number of friendlies being contested yearly, skipped the 2025/26 edition as North American teams focus on their World Cup preparations.

At this point, it's not known when the competition will be played, but judging by previous editions, it can be safely assumed that the two-legged quarterfinals will be played in November 2026, while the one-off semifinals and finals will be contested the following March, mirroring the last time this competition was played in 2024/25.
U.S. Soccer announced in late 2025 that it was permanently moving the annual January camp to December, meaning the early 2026 edition of the traditional meetup is being effectively skipped.

Every year, the USMNT convenes for either one or two international friendlies outside the traditional FIFA international break. As such, the roster is almost entirely made up of domestic-based players, who are in the middle of their offseason at the time of the camp, as MLS plays from March to November.

Clubs are not required to release players for international duty outside of officially designated international breaks, and therefore most European-based players would not be available for action at this time.
Convening in December instead of January affords players less conflict with their club's preseason ramp-up.

articles.headline: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Ole Miss Rebels
keyFacts: The Texas Longhorns will host the seventh-ranked Ole Miss Rebels in a critical game on Saturday night following a two-game losing streak.
Longhorns Wire staff writers predicted losses for Texas, with two picking Ole Miss to win and one predicting an Ole Miss victory.
Writers noted that Texas faces mounting pressure and must deliver a complete performance to overcome their recent struggles and injuries.
body: The term "must-win game" is thrown around a lot in sports. A true must-win game is one that staves off elimination. Well, that's essentially what the Longhorns face Saturday night when Texas hosts the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium.

Just three weeks ago, the Longhorns were the No. 1 team in the nation. Now Texas is fighting for its College Football Playoff life. Steve Sarkisian has gone from the savior of the program to the hottest seat in America. And Arch Manning has gone from superstar to punchline.

It has all gone so wrong so quickly. But Mississippi provides an opportunity for the entire Longhorns football program to put the past two weeks behind it and become the contender they're supposed to be ... on paper at least.
We discussed after the Ohio State game that this Longhorns team might only play all-out and all-in when pushed the the brink . This is the brink.
Tommy Bresee's Prediction

Texas is staring down what seems to be a must-win vs. Ole Miss . The offense has given little reason for confidence and the defense, likely without Colin Simmons, has to contain one of the best QBs in the country. For Texas to end their losing streak streak, they'll need their most complete performance of the season.
It's difficult for me to see them mustering that, especially against Chambliss, Lacy and the Rebels offensive attack.
Final Score: Ole Miss 31, Texas 21
Jamie Gatlin's Prediction
The Longhorns enter their matchup with Ole Miss this weekend on a two-game losing streak. Of late they have been plagued by sloppy play and injuries.

Life won't get any easier against an Ole Miss team ranked seventh in the nation. The Longhorns have shown they have the talent to be an elite team but are now full of question marks. To beat the Rebels they will need to turn things around quickly but he last two weeks have not inspired alot of confidence.
Final Score: Ole Miss 24, Texas 17
Trey Luerssen's Prediction
I really don't know what to think of this team anymore.

Could Texas rise from the ashes like a pheonix and play like the contender everyone thought the were? Or will the Longhorns lose three straight games and have one of the biggest falls any No. 1 team in the nation has ever had?
Will UT figure out enough of its issues to play well and beat a playoff-calibre team in Ole Miss? Or will the entire Steve Sarkisian/Arch Manning era come crashing down on the DKR turf.
The smart money is on the later. Texas and Manning has looked completely lost for two weeks. Desperation can be a great motivator.
Final Score: Ole Miss 24, Texas 27

articles.headline: Battlefield 6 Quietly Yanks Planned Mass Effect Collab From Its Store After BioWare Closure
keyFacts: Fans discovered that Battlefield 6 planned to add Mass Effect cosmetics for N7 Day following the closure of developer BioWare.
Battlefield 6 removed the planned Mass Effect cosmetics from its in-game store without explanation after the studio closure announcement.
Publisher EA has not yet commented on the removal of the Mass Effect items from the game.
body: Battlefield 6 has collaborated with Mass Effect before, and the last time that the military shooter did so, it was shortly after publisher EA gutted BioWare in 2025. To say it felt in bad taste at the time is an understatement. Recently, fans discovered that Battlefield 6 was again seemingly going to add a handful of Mass Effect cosmetics to the game, presumably for N7 Day, BioWareâs annual celebration of its sci-fi RPG series. Now, it appears that the previously locked cosmetics have been removed from the game entirely following the announcement that EA is shutting down the studio.
There's new Mass Effect accessories for Battlefield, probably for N7 Day ð pic.twitter.com/n7cAHFUSHz
— Kala Elizabeth #SaveMassEffect (@kalaelizabeth) October 13, 2026

The cosmetics included several N7 logos in patches and on weapons, as well as a charm of the Normandy, Commander Shepardâs ship in the original trilogy. At some point after the news of BioWareâs closure, these items were removed from Battlefield 6âs in-game store with no explanation. Weâve reached out to EA for comment on the situation and will update this story if we hear back.

Odds are someone at Battlefield Studios or EA had the good sense to realize that releasing something Mass Effect-related right after the company had uprooted the lives of the people who made those games would have been a PR nightmare, especially if they planned to release them on N7 Day, a day when fans and the studio typically celebrated the nearly 20-year-old series. Though some fans say they still would have wanted these items as a way of remembering the studio and its games, I canât imagine it would have been worth the stink it would have caused so soon after the closure of BioWare.Â

Still, while someone may have yanked this off the assembly line, I canât imagine that EAâs good judgement is going to last forever. In all this mess, itâs been reported that Amazonâs Mass Effect TV series is still in the works, just one example of EA continuing to profit from BioWareâs world while the people who made these games have been kicked to the curb without a job and left unable to finish Mass Effect: Universe, the fifth game in the series and one theyâd spent years working on. If EA is still putting out Mass Effect projects now that BioWare is gone, whatâs to stop the company and its private equity overlords from finding other ways to drag the corpse of BioWare around? Maybe weâll see Mass Effect skins in Fortnite to tie in to the release of the show, or maybe EA will just keep raking in the cash from the still-running BioWare merch store featuring the studioâs characters and iconography.Â

For now, itâs probably in EAâs best interest to cancel any N7 Day plans and pretend none of this happened, but make no mistake, these ghouls are just waiting for enough time to pass that the general public forgets what has happened so it can get back to selling you N7-branded guns and t-shirts.

articles.headline: How to get and use fulton drop markers in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4
keyFacts: Fulton drop markers in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode act as portable extraction points.
Players can obtain them through the deluxe edition, by reaching max rank level 70, or by finding them as rare loot and crafting them.
Using a marker calls in a care package with a rope to safely extract from the map without enemy interference.
body: Fulton drop markers in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode are essentially portable exfil points. They're categorized as ultra loot though, which is the rarest tier in the game, making them extremely hard to get your hands on. Some players have them early, however, thanks to the deluxe edition of the game granting them via a survival starter kit.
If you're wondering how to use fulton drop markers and how to get more of them in Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode, here's what you need to know.
How to get fulton drop markers in DMZ

As mentioned above, if you have the deluxe edition of Modern Warfare 4, you'll have two fulton drop markers waiting for you at the survival kits station at your FOB, as part of a starter kit. Once you reach DMZ level 70, aka max rank, you'll unlock the advanced SERE survival kit, which also has fulton drop markers in it.

Otherwise, you'll need to find the fulton drop marker recipe as random loot. If you're lucky enough to have found the fulton drop marker recipe and got it back to your FOB safely, you can craft them at your 3D printer. You just need one prototype RF module (found by looting deathstalkers), three comms modules, and five control units.
For the best chances of finding the recipe, head to high threat areas, as that's where you'll find the rarest loot. Examples include the Haneul Nuclear Reactor, Chang-San Air Base, and The Grid.
Of course, this also goes for fulton drop markers themselves, as they can also be found as standard loot inside containers.
How to use fulton drop markers in DMZ

When you use one, it calls in a care package wherever you throw it. Interact with the care package to activate the exfil, which is a long rope tied to a plane. Stand next to the rope when the countdown ends and you'll immediately exfil, without any risk of being shot at by enemies. This is a huge benefit compared to having to travel to one of a few pre-determined exfil points on the map, which are often PvP hotspots.

articles.headline: Nacon announces the Revolution Pro X – Special Edition, a new Hell Is Us-inspired Xbox controller offering 'joystick tension adjustment, Hall Effect sensors, and micro-switch combine technologies'
keyFacts: Nacon announced the Revolution Pro X – Special Edition, an officially licensed Xbox wireless controller inspired by the game Hell Is Us.
The controller features joystick tension adjustment, Hall Effect sensors, micro-switches, and is available now for £109.99 / $129.90 / €129.99.
Nacon accessories division director Yannick Allaert said the device was designed to offer a full-featured precision controller at a competitive price.
body: - Nacon reveals its officially licensed Xbox controller, the Revolution Pro X – Special Edition
- The controller design is inspired by Hell Is Us and is now available for £109.99 / $129.90 / €129.99
- It combines mechanical fine-tuning for all playstyles and tournament-grade precision
Nacon has announced the Revolution Pro X – Special Edition, its new officially licensed Xbox wireless controller inspired by Rogue Factor's action-adventure game, Hell Is Us.

Revolution Pro X – Special Edition is designed for competitive gaming and combines mechanical tuning and tournament-grade precision, allowing players on PC, Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One, and Smart TVs to customize controls to suit their playstyle.

Available now at NaconGaming for £109.99 / $129.90 / €129.99, the jet-black controller features a minimalist whorl design inspired by Hell Is Us and features contactless Hall Effect joysticks and instant triggers equipped with micro-switches "without mechanical wear," plus two programmable shortcut buttons on the back.
It also offers four vibration motors, two programmable rear buttons, a 2.4 GHz wireless dongle, and a 3 m detachable braided USB-C cable.
"Its control ring lets you adjust the mechanical tension of the joysticks with a single gesture to prioritize either fast movements or precise aiming, depending on the situation," Nacon said.
When connected to a PC, it offers a wired mode with a 1,000 Hz polling rate and matches a claimed latency of 1 ms, prioritizing responsiveness in fast-paced games like first-person shooters.
"With the Revolution Pro X – SE, we wanted to offer a full-featured precision controller at a competitive price,” says Yannick Allaert, director of Nacon's accessories division.

Following recent media reports in Italy and abroad, I feel it is appropriate to clarify my position.

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler insists he remains fully focused on his own job and has the utmost respect for the work “great human being” Michael Carrick is doing at Manchester United.
A humiliating 4-1 loss away to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night and the criticism from captain Bruno Fernandes which followed has put further scrutiny on Carrick’s position.

Following the Seagulls’ fine start to the new campaign, Hurzeler is one of the names touted as a possible replacement for Carrick at Old Trafford should the club decide to make another managerial change.

The German coach, though, maintains he is only thinking about how to keep Brighton moving forward into this weekend’s game at Liverpool, with his side held to a goalless draw in the Conference League away to Czech minnows Jablonec on Thursday night.
“I am really focused on my job here,” Hurzeler said at a press conference. “I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days.

“Beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick, for what he has done with Manchester United at the end of last season. He is a great human being, he is a great personality. Every time we meet each other, we have a really good relationship, so therefore I really respect him and there is nothing more to say about that.” Press Association
Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start

Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race.

Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor.

Gross was moving from Brighton to Borussia Dortmund after seven years in the Premier League and reported to his boyhood club for pre-season training days later. Running is an obsession for Gross, as it is for his former teammate James Milner, who revealed last month he was training for a marathon after finally hanging up his boots, and that has shown since he returned for a second spell at the Amex in January for a bargain £1.2m.
Read Ed Aarons’ feature on Brighton’s hard-working midfielder:
A stadium selfie could soon cost fans of German giants Borussia Dortmund after the club announced plans to reward those who leave their phones alone during the game.

Dortmund are offering signed jerseys and gift cards for club merchandise to fans who use an app which measures how often they unlock their phones at its stadium. Arguing that “more and more fans are annoyed by selfies, streaming, and social media in the stands,” Dortmund say supporters can opt to use a “fan mode” in the club’s app, starting Saturday with a home game against Eintracht Frankfurt. The rewards scheme and app are entirely voluntary and there’s no ban on fans using their phones.

Fan mode will measure how often the phone is unlocked during the game — not counting the halftime break — and award points to people based on how little they use the device, with prizes on offer for those with the most points. Each time the phone is unlocked, the user loses points.
“Over 81,000 people in the stadium, singing, cheering, and holding their breath together: this here and now is irreplaceable,” said Dortmund chief executive Carsten Cramer.
The club’s stance is part of a backlash in German football against attempts to turn its stadium atmosphere into social media content, especially by influencers using professional camera equipment.
Hertha Berlin said this month it was banning “commercially produced and monetized” video productions from its games, while allowing fans to take photos and videos for personal use.

Another club, Dynamo Dresden, said in August it would ban commercial filming for social media, saying it wanted to ensure fans felt comfortable at the game and to protect the club’s TV rights deals. Agence France-Presse

The ongoing security situation in Saudi Arabia makes it difficult for the country to host next year’s Asian Cup as scheduled, according to Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, president of the Japanese Football Association.

Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, raising doubts over whether the continental soccer tournament can take place as scheduled in January and February next year.

“Based on what I’ve learnt from the news, the situation is still unsafe, so at this point, I don’t think it would be easy to hold the AFC (Asian) Cup there,” Miyamoto told reporters at the Asian Football Confederation’s (AFC) extraordinary congress in Tokyo.
“I just had a meeting with the Saudi side and they said that their top priority is the safety of the players, the fans, and everyone who would be attending the tournament.
“They said they would work with the AFC to decide whether the tournament can go ahead, so they did mention that it would take some time (to make that decision).“

AFC chief Salman bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa said last week a postponement until 2028 remained a possibility if necessary, but the local organising committee later said it was sticking to the original schedule. Reuters

Frank Lampard has been talking about Frank Lampard’s Coventry ahead of the Sky Blues early-season basement battle with Fulham. Namely, Lampard has been talking up the work ethic of Gus Hamer after the 29-year-old rejoined Coventry from Sheffield United in the summer for a reported £6million.

So far, fan-favourite Hamer been restricted to four appearances off the bench on his return to the Premier League. Following his latest cameo role in Monday night’s 3-1 defeat at Tottenham, Hamer asked to play for the under-21s on Tuesday lunch-time and Lampard was impressed. “He wanted to play. It was a personal decision and I like that,” Lampard said at his pre-match press conference. “He wanted to play and get minutes because Gus has been used to playing minutes regularly, pretty much.
“And these days at Coventry from his days at Sheffield United we’ve got a competitive squad now and his area of the pitch is competitive.

“But Gus has been very, very good to work with since he’s come back to us. Myself and my staff have been really, really impressed by his approach, his training, his ethic and what he wants to do. And Gus is going to help us.

“We all know, everyone in the building and at the CBS knows that he’s a really talented player who’s going to help us. So he’s just staying ready, and I’m very pleased with how Gus has been. He’s a good example.”
Hello, happy Friday. Have we had football every day this week? I think we have… Monday night football, three nights of European games and now Friday night at Portman Road. What a world.

“Surely the most popular request for Uniteds new stadium will be ‘seats facing the other way’?” honks Tim Woods. I have to say, as a stadium nerd and stadium aesthete, that were I given a vote I’d opt to mothball the whole thing as it’s quite the ugliest new arena design I’ve seen in a while.

Álvaro Arbeloa’s been talking ahead of Fulham’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, and buoyed up by last weekend’s much needed win over Hull. “Nothing has changed for us,” insisted the manager, “we were not winning games but we believed in ourselves, we were doing so many things well,

“The most important thing [about the Hull win] is we were in same situation against Manchester United and Ipswich but didn’t win but now we had to improve in our transition and did. We controlled the ball in their half better than before.”

As for that first win lifting pressure off him, Arbeloa said: “It’s not about me, it’s about my players and the supporters because they were behind us and the players because of the work they’ve done.”

In Spain, it’s the Clásico on Sunday at the Camp Nou, with leaders Barcelona having made the better start to the season, though Real Madrid – six points behind – have begun to hit their straps. But is it still the world’s biggest match? Here’s Graham Ruthven:

As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture?

Sunday’s match at Camp Nou will be watched by hundreds of millions of viewers all over the world. A clásico always carries significance, but this weekend’s edition will be especially significant. A Barça win would move them nine points clear of their rivals at the top of La Liga. A Real Madrid victory could be a catalyst for the rest of their season.

At the risk of sucking all the air out of the room with more Manchester United chat, Marco Rose has inevitably been asked for his two pennorth given his Bournemouth side visit Old Trafford on Sunday. And he reckons his buoyant side will face “angry and intense” opponents. “I’m quite sure [Michael Carrick] will tell his players it’s all about mentality, effort and attitude,” said Rose. “You hear all the voices and noises but I don’t know it helps us and it’s up to us to go there and be focused, react well. They’re going to be angry and intense and we have to face it.”
Three games ago we were talking about Bournemouth possibly having a bit of a hangover season – and they’re still lowly placed in the Premier League – but they’re pretty perky right now.
Manchester United are inviting fans to offer their views via a survey on the design of the proposed new 100,000-seat stadium.

Colette Roche, United’s CEO New Stadium Development, said: “Our proposed new stadium is one of the most significant projects Manchester United will undertake in the next 100 years, and it is vital that we shape it together with our fans. Above all else, this is a football stadium built for them, so getting the details right matters.”

Supporters have until 6 November to take the survey, with subjects including: “creating a world-class football stadium and match-day experience for all fans”; “heritage and legacy”; “atmosphere”; “the wider campus”; and “getting to and from the stadium.”

The survey will be sent to season ticket holders, cup season ticket holders, executive club members, official members, supporters who have purchased hospitality at Old Trafford within the past three years and season ticket waiting list members, a press release stated.

It’s north London derby day in the Women’s Super League tomorrow, with Arsenal arriving at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium under considerable pressure after their poor start. Derby passions will run high with Spurs’ Cathinka Tandberg, for one, bang up for it, as she explains in this interview with Sophie Downey:

“It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday.
“It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.”

“All the Spurs fans hate Arsenal and Arsenal hate Spurs. That’s how it is. You want to show that you’re the best team. Simple as that. You just want to fight for the club, the badge and for the people around you.”
Wilcox wants Howe if Manchester United replace Carrick
Jamie Jackson
The noise continues. Eddie Howe is the under-fire Jason Wilcox’s choice as next cab off the rank should Michael Carrick be binned. Jamie Jackson has all the latest:

Eddie Howe is the current preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox to replace Michael Carrick should Manchester United decide to change manager, with the director of football believing Howe’s extensive Premier League experience places him ahead of other potential targets.
Howe left Newcastle in late July to take a break from the game but would seriously consider a return for the United role, it is understood, should this be offered.

In Manchester City on-field news, Erling Haaland is back fit to face Aston Villa at Villa Park tomorrow, PA reports. The Norway striker was not risked in City’s Champions League victory over AEK Athens in midweek after a blow to the foot in the previous game against Ipswich.

City will continue to assess Nico O’Reilly, Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes, who also suffered knocks in the same game. The manager, Enzo Maresca, said: “They could all be available or not. There are still doubts. Erling is the only one who is 100 per cent available and for the other three we need to wait.”
Jonathan Liew’s column on how Brazil’s footballing and political dysfunction feed each other is a good read:

We hear a lot about football’s power to unite a nation. Perhaps we underestimate the extent to which it can also divide; the way it can reflect the very worst of ourselves, our greed and vindictiveness, our lust for feuds and, petty entertainment. There is a Women’s World Cup being hosted in Brazil next summer and while Lula has sought to fast-track the professionalisation of women’s football, Bolsonaro’s only public utterances in the field of women’s sport have been to assert his opposition to trans athletes playing it.
In courage of their convictions news, the Asian Football Confederation has decided to endorse Gianni Infantino’s Fifa presidential re-election bid.

The AFC president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

“We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the Fifa president.” Sheikh Salman said. “You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well.”

Morning everyone. What about them Cherries eh? Before we dive deep into weekend previews, Manchester United melodramas and what have you, some moments to reflect on last night’s action. Chief among them was the continuation of Bournemouth’s European fairytale – a deserved 3-0 Europa League shellacking of Milan, a result barely conceivable two decades ago, but, as Nick Ames sagely points out in his match report, not a great surprise given the resources even mid-ranking Premier League clubs can now command compared to fading Serie A giants.

Elsewhere, Sunderland dug in for a draw at Lech Poznan, Crystal Palace’s mixed start to Europa League life continued in a 2-2 draw at Besiktas, and … oh Celtic. A third European defeat on the spin for Martin O’Neill’s side as they surrendered a 1-0 lead to lose the Celt derby 2-1 to Celta Vigo, who brought 3,000 fans to Glasgow – reportedly their biggest ever European away turnout – for a cultural love-in.

Anyway, we’ll have pre-match news, interviews and comment through the day, and feel free to mail in your thoughts. Off to a game this weekend? Tell us your hopes for it. In the meantime, to get in the mood, here’s 10 English top-flight things to look out for.

articles.headline: Vote now: The Mammoth Tank and Priest go head-to-head to determine the best RTS unit of all time
keyFacts: PC Gamer is holding a month-long tournament to determine the greatest real-time strategy unit of all time.
The Mammoth Tank from Red Alert and the Priest from Age of Empires are competing in the final round.
Readers have until the end of Wednesday BST to vote, and the winner will be announced next week.
body: Our month-long RTS tournament is coming to an end. We started with a shortlist of 16 units, and now we're down to the final two—both of which were determined by your votes. This is what democracy is all about, folks! Determining what RTS unit has the right to call itself the greatest unit of all time.

It's been an emotional journey. Dreams shattered. Friendships ruined. Drug tests performed on a member of the clergy. But this is important, worthwhile work. But let's stop faffing around and get stuck in.
The final bracket
Well, it looks like my prediction from last week did not come to pass. A tragedy!

With the humble Peon failing to return from the dead, I was left with only one of my original picks in the running: the unstoppable Pride of Hiigara from Homeworld 2. As it turns out, it's actually quite stoppable. The indomitable Mammoth Tank from Red Alert gave it a beating, winning with 60% of the votes.

I will gracefully accept this defeat. I mean c'mon, the Mammoth Tank is a legend. Could it realistically destroy a mothership that can spit out a fleet of capital ships? Probably not! But this tournament is not determining which unit would win in a fight. "The best" can mean a lot of different things, and there's no denying the Mammoth Tank is awesome.

I do, however, take umbrage with the Priest defeating the Super Star Destroyer. 70% of the votes! This is madness. That wololo-ing thief has no honour. But even though this outcome is ridiculous, I must accept the will of the people. I just hope that was the horrible little man's last victory.
So we're down to two. Mammoth Tank vs Priest. I'm going to give you all until the end of Wednesday (BST) to vote. Can this icon of the Soviet war machine defeat God's pal? We'll find out next week.
Mammoth Tank vs Priest
Mammoth Tank (Command and Conquer: Red Alert)
God bless these great, trundling beasts—implacable Soviet strength wrought in steel and pig iron.

Mammoth Tanks are unfathomably costly and painfully slow, but whatever. I'm convinced just one of them could probably win the entire RA1 Soviet campaign by itself. Akh-knowledged. —Joshua Wolens, News Writer
Priest (Age of Empires)
"Wololo." I win. —Jody Macgregor, Weekend Editor

Fraser is the UK online editor and has actually met The Internet in person. With over a decade of experience, he's been around the block a few times, serving as a freelancer, news editor and prolific reviewer. Strategy games have been a 30-year-long obsession, from tiny RTSs to sprawling political sims, and he never turns down the chance to rave about Total War or Crusader Kings. He's also been known to set up shop in the latest MMO and likes to wind down with an endlessly deep, systemic RPG. These days, when he's not editing, he can usually be found writing features that are 1,000 words too long or talking about his dog.

articles.headline: As a lifelong 76ers fan, I am glad Trump blasted LeBron James for disrespecting the national anthem
keyFacts: Philadelphia 76ers player LeBron James moved his hips and mimicked a golf swing and shooting during the national anthem at a game against the New York Knicks.
President Donald Trump criticized James on Truth Social and during a rally, calling him a disgrace and demanding an apology.
The article's author expressed agreement with Trump's criticism, arguing that James's behavior during the anthem was disrespectful.
body: As a lifelong Philadelphia 76ers fan, I had mixed emotions when the team signed NBA superstar LeBron James as a free agent over the summer. On one hand, he is an immense NBA talent and megastar, and this kind of thing doesn’t happen to the Sixers franchise, ever. And even though he is in the twilight of his career at 41 years old, James’s recent level of productivity, combined with the team-friendly contract he signed, instantly makes the team a title contender. My reservations, however, stemmed from the fact that he is just so darn unlikable and a staunch left-wing political acolyte.
And James took less than one game in a Sixers uniform to validate my concerns.

During the performance of the national anthem at Tuesday night’s nationally televised season opener against the defending NBA champions, the New York Knicks, at Madison Square Garden, James refused to remain still, unlike every other player on the court. Instead, he started swinging his hips in a semicircular motion while holding his hands wide, making a movement resembling a golf swing. He then mimicked shooting a basketball multiple times. To say it was extremely odd behavior during the national anthem would be an understatement.
As a lifelong @sixers fan, I’m quite glad Trump called out LeBron James for this disrespect. https://t.co/QbCGVO5IOX
— Christopher Tremoglie (@chriswtremo) October 23, 2026
But more importantly, it was disrespectful, and President Donald Trump noticed the slight. The president took to Truth Social to scold the Sixers’ prized free agent signing.

“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump said . “LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!”

I actually couldn’t agree more. I am glad Trump called out James for his behavior. My first reaction upon seeing it was that he was being completely disrespectful to the national anthem. At worst, it looked like he was subliminally engaging in anti-patriotic behavior. At best, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, who has played in the league for over 23 years, is just so obtuse and self-centered that he either thinks he can do whatever he wants or doesn’t realize what professional basketball players are supposed to be doing during the performance of the national anthem. Either way, it is not a good look.

It’s not the first time James has encountered controversy during the performance of the national anthem. In 2020, while with the Los Angeles Lakers, James knelt during the national anthe m while wearing a shirt that read “Black Lives Matter.” It was another sign of disrespect toward the country and the national anthem, but it also signified that James understood their importance and relevance. Doing those stretches at that particular time is just inexcusable and dishonorable behavior. Trump is right to say James should apologize. He won’t, for a variety of reasons, but Trump is correct nevertheless.
The president renewed his criticism of James during a campaign rally in Sioux City, Iowa, on Thursday night.

“And what about LeBron James? Did you see that deal?” Trump said. “No, he’s doing, during the national anthem, he’s practicing his golf swing,” he said while mimicking James’s actions. “I said, ‘What the hell is that?’”
“It’s a big scandal kind of a story,” the president added. “I don’t understand it.”
JOSH SHAPIRO TOO COWARDLY TO DENOUNCE BLACK MAN’S RACISM IN ALLEGED KILLING OF WHITE PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER

Again, Trump is right. But this is also why Trump is so beloved and why he is different from any other president before him, especially among Republicans. No other president would have enough guts to criticize a megastar professional athlete for disrespecting the country and the national anthem. A Democratic president wouldn’t do it because they wouldn’t care. A Republican president would be too scared of the fallout and would go apoplectic worrying about being called racist.

Meanwhile, Trump bows to no one and doesn’t succumb to the political will or threats of the rabid Left. Trump does what he thinks is right, and in this case, that means criticizing LeBron James. His criticism of James warrants praise and should be revered because, once he is out of office, it is unlikely that another president will have the character, integrity, and fearlessness to mount such defenses of our national anthem and American pride.

articles.headline: Trump to rally in Florida after stoking Ramaswamy ad furor – US politics live
keyFacts: Donald Trump said he told Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy to continue running an attack ad against his Democratic rival.
Republican candidate Ashley Hinson condemned the ad and said it should be taken down, breaking with Trump.
Trump will hold a campaign rally in Fort Myers, Florida, to support gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds.
body: Trump to rally in Florida amid growing outcry over Ramaswamy attack ad
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of US politics. Donald Trump is travelling to Florida today to speak at another rally as midterm election day races nearer.

The president will stump for gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds. Whether Donalds regards this as helpful remains to be seen after he removed mentions of the president from his website and has barely uttered his name during the race for governor.
My colleague Richard Luscombe has more on that race:

Last night, Trump further stoked the controversy over an attack ad by Vivek Ramaswamy, featuring the mother of his Democratic rival, Dr Amy Acton – telling supporters at a rally that he personally told the Republican candidate for Ohio governor to keep running the spot.
Acton’s mother lost custody of her daughter at age 12 because her husband was charged with raping the young girl. Trump told the rally in Iowa: “I said, ‘You’ve got to ride with it.’”

Trump looks increasingly out of step with his own party over the ad after yet another Republican denounced the ad on Thursday. Iowa Republican Senate candidate Ashley Hinson broke with the president by denouncing the attack ad, saying: “I think it’s absolutely terrible, and I think they should take the ad down.”

A data leak from Germany’s far-right German Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) has revealed the extent of efforts by the party to court Donald Trump and other leading figures in the Maga movement, stretching back more than a decade.

The trove reveals the pains the AfD took in wooing the president, whom they saw from the beginning as a potential ally, with senior party officials agonising over the wording of an obsequious congratulatory telegram when he was elected in 2016, which included the wish that his “hopes as a person be fulfilled”.
Trump hailed the win in Saxony-Anhalt in a post on his Truth Social, concluding his message with a German version of his Make America Great Again acronym, “MGGA!!!”
The leaked documents show AfD officials quickly moving to requests for support from the White House on policy issues when he first won the 2016 election.
Others show a burgeoning political courtship between senior figures including the AfD’s now leader Alice Weidel and key Trump ideologue Steve Bannon.

The data, provided to reporters by the transparency organisation Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), covers more than 420,000 emails, along with documents and personnel records, from the party’s foundation in 2013 to the present, with most coming before 2019.
The ongoing slowdown to Ukraine’s access to Starshield – the modified military-grade version of the Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite network – reached fever pitch this week.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the Donald Trump had asked Musk to restore the service, with Trump later told reporters the system was “back”.

However, the president refused to comment on whether he had spoken to Musk, but appeared to suggest the ultimate power to limit the service rested with the SpaceX founder and CEO. “I guess the bottom line, he put it back,” Trump said, referring to Musk.
This comes after a protracted series of disruptions for Ukraine accessing the network – a key defense tool against Russian strikes.
Despite Trump’s insistence, Ukrainian officials said on Friday morning that speeds remained capped, with no indication that the restrictions had been lifted.

Trump will begin his day in Washington, before his midterms blitz continues in Florida. A reminder that today is his fifth day of campaign rallies this week. He’ll deliver remarks at 2pm ET in Fort Myers.

We mentioned the key gubernatorial race in the Sunshine state earlier – where Republican congressman Byron Donalds will face off against Democrat David Jolly. But there is also a key contest that we’re watching in Florida too.
This is the special Senate election, where the Republican incumbent, Ashley Moody, is facing a challenge from progressive Democrat Angie Nixon – who defied odds and won her primary earlier this year.

Americans heading to the polls for next month’s midterm elections are not just choosing whom to send to Washington, or their state capitols. There are also 145 statewide measures on ballots across 39 states, polling voters on actions from a novel wealth tax on California’s billionaires to requiring Alabama’s public schools to broadcast or perform the first stanza of the national anthem each week.

Voters in Idaho, Nevada and Virginia are asked to protect abortion rights; voters in Missouri are asked to give those rights back. Property tax issues appear on dozens of state ballots. Several state referendums ask voters to bar trans athletes from competing in women’s sports, or bar gender-affirming medical care for minors.

Voters like referendums, in principle, as a tool of direct democracy. “Polls in every state show at least 2-to-1 support for having an initiative process,” said John Matsusaka, a business professor at the University of Southern California (USC) and executive director of the Initiative and Referendum Institute.

Speaking to ABC News, Hinson said: “It’s terrible. I think about it as a mom and you think about your kids surviving childhood sexual abuse and having to relive that trauma on TV again.”
Hinson also criticised vice-president JD Vance for striking “absolutely the wrong tone” when he said he was “disgusted” by Republicans “whining” about the ad.
“Iowans want - and probably Ohioans want – someone who’s going to be an empathetic leader, and I think it sends absolutely the wrong message.

“And I would bet that Amy Acton and I probably don’t agree on anything, either. But like the last thing I would want as someone who’s running against is to force them to relive the childhood trauma. So, I think, again, I think it’s wrong, and it should come down.

articles.headline: Blair and LaCivita try to repair damage of Bosnia contracts with Trump library donation
keyFacts: James Blair and Chris LaCivita donated their consulting fees from Bosnia and Herzegovina to President Donald Trump's presidential library fund.
The donation follows public criticism from Trump after reports revealed the advisers provided election advice to a Russia-friendly territory.
Construction on Trump's presidential library tower and museum in Miami is expected to begin near the end of 2027.
body: James Blair and Chris LaCivita confirmed Thursday that they donated their controversial consulting fees from work in Bosnia and Herzegovina to President Donald Trump’s presidential library fund.

Blair and LaCivita, who jointly managed Trump’s successful 2024 presidential campaign and worked for his MAGA Inc. PAC, faced the president’s public ire earlier this month after reports surfaced that they had advised a Russia -friendly political territory in the Balkan nation while continuing to work on Republican political efforts in the United States.
Blair confirmed the donation following a report by the New York Post , saying the two advisers had given up their entire payment from the consulting work.

“Yes, it’s true we donated our full fee,” Blair wrote on social media. “I love the President and am eternally grateful for the opportunities he has provided me. Contributing to the preservation of his legacy of greatness is my honor!”
Yes, it’s true we donated our full fee. I love the President and am eternally grateful for the opportunities he has provided me.
Contributing to the preservation of his legacy of greatness is my honor! https://t.co/2egh6FPHyE
— James Blair (@JamesBlairUSA) October 23, 2026
LaCivita touted the donation is a separate social media post, saying “preserving the legacy and story of @realDonaldTrump is an honor and a no brainer!”
Trump had distanced himself from the two advisers in a Truth Social post on Oct. 7, emphasizing that they were not his employees.

“Chris LaCivita and James Blair are outside consultants,” Trump wrote. “They do not work for me, other than as outside consultants. They most likely have numerous clients, but for that, you would have to ask them.”

The president’s remarks followed a New York Times report that Blair and LaCivita had traveled to Republika Srpska, a self-governing entity within Bosnia and Herzegovina, to provide election advice. The two were reportedly paid hundreds of thousands of dollars through a Washington law firm retained by the territory’s government.

Republika Srpska has longstanding political ties to Russia, and its leadership has pursued greater autonomy from Bosnia and Herzegovina’s central government. The territory’s political leadership has also faced international scrutiny over its separatist rhetoric and challenges to the country’s constitutional order.

The consulting work raised questions about the advisers’ outside business activities as they remained involved in Republican politics ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Blair served as a deputy chief of staff in the Trump administration until May, while LaCivita has continued to work as a prominent Republican political strategist.

articles.headline: Trump's U.N. envoy says Iran war could drag on for another year
keyFacts: U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz said the war with Iran could last another year, though he hopes Iran comes to negotiations sooner.

Foreign ministers from seven nations will meet Friday in Istanbul to discuss the Strait of Hormuz conflict and regional stability.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz has told the Financial Times the could last another year, but the Trump administration envoy said he hopes the Iranians "come to the table" before that.

- The price of Brent crude oil hit $114 a barrel Friday after Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed to have disabled seven tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump of lying about attacks on ships to drive up oil prices before the U.S. midterm elections.

- State-owned energy giant Saudi Aramco said Thursday that the amount of oil flowing through its East-West pipeline, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, had more than tripled from 2 million to 7 million barrels per day, as uncertainty hangs over exports across the Middle East.
UAE resident describes smelling gas after oil tanker spill
Residents in the north of the United Arab Emirates have described smelling gas after an oil spill off the country's coastline.
Many Emiratis have reported chemical smells on social media in recent days, including residents in northern districts of Dubai, the largest city in the UAE.
"For the past two days it smelled like 10 gas stations spilled their gas everywhere," a Sharjah resident told the AFP news agency, asking to remain anonymous.
"I was on my balcony and panicked thinking gas was leaking in my house and I will blow up everyone."
Emirati authorities "detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain's beaches," the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said in a statement Friday, referring to an emirate north of Dubai.

News of the spill came a day after Iran claimed to have struck four commercial vessels in Persian Gulf waters and said three others had hit sea mines in the region, though President Trump has accused Tehran of making up the incidents to drive up oil prices.
CBS/AFP
Iranian state TV claims movement of "non-compliant" vessels in Strait of Hormuz completely halted

Iranian state TV claimed Friday, citing an unnamed source close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy, that all movement of "non-compliant" vessels through the Strait of Hormuz had been completely halted following a series of Iranian attacks on ships and navigational support systems.

The report cited the source as saying that if U.S. military escorts and ship-to-ship transfers - all of which the Iranian regime refers to as "oil smuggling" - resumes, action against the vessels and technical systems supporting them will be "much more forceful."

Iran has repeatedly warned commercial ships not to use the long-established shipping lanes through the strait, through which about 20% of global oil supplies passed before the war. Tehran demands that all vessels seek authorization and use a northern route, close to its coast, and it has attacked ships for months that refuse.
The Trump administration, however, has encouraged shippers to use an alternative southern route, close to Oman, to avoid Iranian tolls.
Iran claimed Thursday to have struck four ships that used that route, and said three others hit sea mines in the U.S.-designated shipping lanes.
President Trump on Thursday dismissed Iranian claims about striking vessels as lies aimed at increasing global oil prices ahead of the looming U.S. midterm elections.
Both Iran and the U.S. have claimed at various times during the war to have completely halted traffic that violates their respective blockades of the waterway.
Iran's foreign minister calls Israel's relationship with the U.S. "parasitic"
Iran's foreign minister has called Israel's relationship with the United States "parasitic," citing alleged American taxpayer funding for missile defense in Israel.

"The U.S. has over the past three years spent $11 BILLION in taxpayer money on missile defense for Israel," Abbas Araghchi wrote Friday in a post on X, citing calculations by independent policy analyst Stephen Semler, who said he arrived at the number using Pentagon budget documents, media reports, and open-source intelligence.
CBS News has not been able to independently verify the figures.

Semler is the founder of the Security Policy Reform Institute, a think tank that, according to its website, is "driven by empiricism and guided by progressive values" to promote "the meaningful reform of U.S. foreign policy to break the cycle of endless war and serve the most pressing economic, social, and political needs of working-class Americans."

Araghchi also said the U.S. had "fired more interceptors defending Israel than Israel has," a claim supported by a Washington Post story from May that cited U.S. Defense Department data and U.S. officials.
"That is not a symbiotic relationship," Araghchi said. "It is a parasitic one."
UAE reports oil spill from tanker

The United Arab Emirates reported an oil spill from a tanker off its coast Friday, a day after Iran claimed to have struck four commercial vessels in Persian Gulf waters and said three others had hit sea mines in the region.
Emirati authorities "detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain's beaches," the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said in a statement, referring to an emirate north of Dubai.
It said "teams immediately began containment, cordoning, clean-up and remediation ... to limit environmental impacts," adding that Umm Al Quwain beaches had been closed.
Many residents in the north of the UAE have reported oil smells on social media in recent days, including residents in northern districts of Dubai.
Frequent attacks on ships have been reported in recent weeks near the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States.

The British maritime security UKMTO reported on Oct. 9 that a vessel was hit by a projectile off the UAE coast, causing a fire that was later brought under control. According to the maritime security company Vanguard, the vessel in question was the Panama-flagged oil tanker GEM NO.2.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed the seven additional incidents on Thursday, but none have been corroborated thus far, and President Trump accused Tehran of inventing strikes on ships to drive up oil prices.
CBS/AFP
Saudi Arabia postpones U.N. summit in Riyadh amid Houthi strikes
Saudi Arabia has postponed the sixth U.N. World Data Forum and the second Saudi Statistical Forum, which had been scheduled to take place in Riyadh next month, until 2027.
The kingdom's General Authority for Statistics said the delay was intended to ensure broad international participation.
It comes after the recent rescheduling of Saudi Arabia's Future Investment Initiative, known as "Davos in the Desert," which was also pushed back to 2027 amid escalating regional tension and .
U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says Iran war could last another year
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz has said the war with Iran could drag on for another year.
In an interview with the Financial Times published Friday, Waltz said the U.S. could still be fighting the war President Trump initially said would last "" 12 months from now.
Waltz told the FT the U.S. will not have achieved its key goals in Iran until the country disposes of its highly enriched uranium and accepts a "meaningful agreement on their domestic enrichment."
"I'm not going to put out hypotheticals. One would hope that they'll come to the table in a meaningful way before that," Waltz said, referring to the possibility of another year of war.

He added that Mr. Trump "and the U.S. Navy can maintain this blockade [on Iranian ports] for the foreseeable future," and said the administration was still "tightening" its economic pressure campaign against Iran.
Mr. Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have renewed their threats to launch new strikes on Iran after the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.
Foreign ministers from Europe and Gulf region to discuss Strait of Hormuz and Iran conflict

Foreign ministers from seven nations in Europe, the Middle East and elsewhere will hold talks in Istanbul Friday focused on the Strait of Hormuz and the interlinked crises in the Middle East, as well as the Ukraine war.

Ministers from the so-called E3 group – Britain, France and Germany – will meet counterparts from the newly created R4 group, composed of Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt, to discuss the Israel-Palestinian crisis, developments in Yemen and the Strait of Hormuz, and ways to end the Russia-Ukraine war, a Turkish foreign ministry source told AFP.

British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband's office said the talks would revolve around "the Strait of Hormuz and the situation in Saudi Arabia," as the in its decade-long civil war, which has flared up amid the U.S. war on Iran.

"Despite positive progress from the U.S. and regional partners, passage through the Strait remains under threat, with traffic through the waterway sharply down on pre-war levels," a U.K. foreign ministry statement said.

It said Miliband would "advocate for a diplomatic solution to the crisis that restores full navigational rights and freedoms" and stress "how Iranian tactics are being replicated across the region, with attacks on Saudi Arabia further destabilizing the region and increasing pressure on vital waterways and global chokepoints, such as Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal."
"The U.K. is stepping up to help stabilize the region, having this week committed RAF Typhoons to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks in their airspace," it added.
CBS/AFP
Saudi Aramco says volume bypassing Strait of Hormuz via pipeline has surged

The president of Saudi state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco, whose facilities have been targeted by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants repeatedly for weeks, says the amount of oil moving through a pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz has more than tripled.
The East-West pipeline's capacity has surged from 2 million to 7 million barrels each day, President and CEO Amin Nasser said in an interview with Saudi-owned television Al Arabiya Business.

Built in the early 1980s, the pipeline has played a crucial role in Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil amid disruption to shipping via the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. It carries crude from Saudi oil fields and production facilities in the east, on the Persian Gulf, to the Yanbu oil terminal on the Saudi Red Sea coast on the other side of the vast kingdom, from which it can be shipped to global markets.

That route, which, unlike the Gulf, has two available exits, has also been threatened and attacked by the Houthis, who have vowed to stop Saudi shipments via the Red Sea's southern gateway, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Nasser said Saudi Aramco has used drones to assess damage caused to infrastructure, including sites key to the East-West pipeline, by Houthi attacks, and to help with firefighting.
CBS/AP
Trump accuses Iran of lying about strikes on ships to drive up oil prices
As crude oil prices hit their highest levels since May, President Trump accused Iran on Thursday of lying about attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz to drive up global energy prices.

"Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social. "They are even making up fake hits, mines, and everything else, because more Oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the Conflict."
Brent crude, the international standard for oil, hit $112 a barrel Thursday morning, its highest price since May 18.

Iran claimed to have struck four vessels in the Persian Gulf Thursday after they transited the Strait of Hormuz using a U.S.-endorsed route that Tehran rejects, and it said three others hit sea mines in the region after using the same shipping lanes. All of the ships were damaged along or after using southern shipping lanes in the strait near the Omani coast, which the Trump administration has insisted for weeks is open to traffic.

The U.S. military has escorted tankers out of the Persian Gulf using that route, boosting the quantity of oil leaving the region, but it is a costly process. Overall instability in the Middle East has kept energy prices high despite the recently increased supplies.

articles.headline: Greece enacts social media ban for kids under 15
keyFacts: Greece passed a law banning social media for children under 15, which will go into effect on January 1, 2027.

body: Greece enacts social media ban for kids under 15
The law is now official and will go into effect on January 1, 2027.

Greece's parliament has passed a social media ban for kids under 15 after its prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis first announced the measure earlier this year. The bill, which Mitsotakis called "difficult but necessary," is among the first to be imposed in the European Union so far and will go into effect on January 1, 2027. The new law covers platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X, and mandates that such services apply proportionate and reliable age-verification methods.

"It would have been very easy to do absolutely nothing today and wait for the perfect European law. But the challenge is here. Children are sinking into the internet every day, and I believe a responsible government must do what it is obliged to do," said Greece's digital governance and AI minister, Dimitris Papastergiou.

Failure to comply with the act will lead to fines under the EU's Digital Services Act. Parents would also need to download apps backed by the state called Kids Wallet or Gov.gr that are paired to their child's device and block access. Those apps, Papastergiou said, are designed to protect privacy and minimize data collected by using "age tokens" that can confirm someone's age while minimizing the disclosure of their personal data.

The legislation was opposed by Greece's minority parties, so Mitsotakis used his majority government to pass the bill. The nation previously barred mobile phones in schools in 2024, and opinion polls show that the new social media ban for children is widely supported by Greece's adult population.

Mitsotakis previously said that his government's "goal is to push the European Union in this direction as well." The European Commission recently introduced the EU Kids Act to do just that, but that law stipulates an outright ban only for children under 13. Australia was the first nation to enact a full social media ban for kids, but the age verification has proved challenging to implement.

articles.headline: El Clasico: All to know about the rivalry between Barcelona and Real Madrid
keyFacts: Barcelona and Real Madrid will play an El Clasico match on Sunday at Camp Nou, with Barcelona entering as league leaders and favorites.
The century-old football rivalry stems from deep political and cultural divisions between Spain's two largest cities, Barcelona and Madrid.
The historical head-to-head record between the two clubs is tied at 106 wins each, alongside 52 draws.
body: The excitement is mounting as El Clasico between Barcelona and Real Madrid approaches.
The rivalry, which spans more than a century, is one of the biggest in world football. On Sunday, both sides will vie to walk away from Camp Nou with bragging rights.
Here’s everything to know about the rivalry:
When did the El Clasico rivalry begin?

The rivalry between Barcelona and Real Madrid dates back to 1902, when the teams first met in the Copa de la Coronacion (a predecessor to the current-day Copa del Rey). Barcelona won the match 3-1 on May 13, 1902, at the La Castellana hippodrome in Madrid.
It took another six meetings before they finally faced each other in La Liga on February 17, 1929. Real won the match 2-1, thanks to Rafael Morera’s brace.
The formation of Spain’s top flight that year added further intensity to the rivalry.
The term El Clasico – “The Classic” in Spanish – first appeared in a local newspaper during the 1960s. By that time, the match had been long considered a huge derby.

The rivalry is now recognised as one of the biggest in world sport and, in the last two decades, has featured the era of Pep Guardiola vs Jose Mourinho in the dugouts and the small matter of Lionel Messi vs Cristiano Ronaldo on the pitch.
How did the El Clasico rivalry begin, and how has it evolved?
Madrid and Barcelona are the two largest cities in Spain – this is at the root of their rivalry, which also has deep political undertones.

In the 1930s, the divide between the two cities deepened. FC Barcelona, founded in 1899, came to symbolise Catalan independence, and Real, which came into existence three years later, represented Spanish nationalism.
The conflict between Real Madrid and Barcelona has long surpassed the sporting dimension, so much that elections to the clubs’ presidencies have been strongly politicised.
In recent times, the two clubs have been in a bitter war of words and ongoing legal disputes.
Earlier this month, Real Madrid submitted a 50,000-page dossier to European football’s governing body, UEFA, urging them to conclude their ongoing investigation into the Negreira case.

The case pertains to Barcelona allegedly paying millions of dollars to the company of Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former vice president of Spanish football’s refereeing committee, between 2001 and 2018, to try to influence referee decisions.
Meanwhile, on Monday, Barcelona President Joan Laporta criticised Real Madrid for “constantly attacking” La Liga.

Real have demanded Javier Tebas’s resignation from his positions as La Liga chief and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation after he compared rhetoric from the club’s management to the propaganda methods used by the Nazi Party in Germany.
Who has dominated El Clasico in recent years?
The overall head-to-head record is tied, with 106 wins each and 52 draws.
If you look at El Clasicos over the last five years, it is a close battle – Barca have won 10 times, while Real have won nine.
Looking at the last 10 clashes, Barca again have a slight edge, winning six times, while Real have four wins.
Who are the favourites in Sunday’s El Clasico?
As the current league leaders, Barcelona are strong favourites to win on Sunday.
Barca have won nine out of nine La Liga matches this season, while Real have lost two and sit third, six points behind Barca.
Should Barca emerge victorious, it would make it two El Clasico wins in a row, following their 2-0 win last season, on May 10.

That result was extra special for the Catalan club as it meant they retained the title, and it marked only the second time the outcome of La Liga had been decided directly by the result of El Clasico.

articles.headline: Texas introduces Bevo Lab: AI-powered game-planning tool also evaluates portal targets, rev-share budgets
keyFacts: Texas announced the Bevo Lab, a new sports analytics and artificial intelligence hub intended to serve all 21 university sports teams.
Texas coaches said early work using Google artificial intelligence tools has saved them more than 15 hours a week in game preparation.
The hub will involve student researchers, with construction expected to finish in three months and full operation targeted for 2027.
body: Texas football coaches spend hours developing game plans every week. Now they have a new voice available at their meetings: a chatbot.

They type questions into their computer and ask an artificial intelligence about tendencies. How often does an opponent blitz on third-and-5 or shorter? Which receiver do they target on third down? Are they more likely to run or pass on third-and-short? Google's Gemini sifts through cloud-stored data, examines it, and provides its findings.
It's a prototype. Soon, it will do much more.

Texas on Friday announced a new sports analytics and artificial intelligence hub on campus called the Bevo Lab, a 25,000-square-foot space inside Austin's Innovation Tower. Google Cloud, Dell Technologies and SHI International are the founding corporate partners for what they believe is the first-of-its-kind hub focused on sports analytics.
"It's not the boogeyman," Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte told CBS Sports. "Let's lean into this. Let's lean into analytics."

Texas says early work with Google Public Sector has saved its coaches more than 15 hours a week in game preparation this season. Kirk Goldsberry, executive director of the Business of Sports Institute at Texas, said the figure comes from the Longhorns' game-planning reports. Google engineers helped rebuild how those reports are produced, digging through what Goldsberry called "haystacks of data."

"They would come in Saturday night or Sunday morning and have their game planning reports ready for big meetings Sunday and Monday," Goldsberry said. "That was a giant pain in the rear end. We were able to streamline some of that."

Goldsberry made his name charting shots in the NBA for ESPN's Grantland, and later served as the San Antonio Spurs' vice president of strategic research and head analyst for Team USA Basketball. He also wrote the New York Times bestseller "SprawlBall."
"The biggest mystery here is why did it take so, so freaking long for this to happen at a university?" he said.

Goldsberry has hired 24 undergraduate students for Bevo Lab's first team, and they begin training with Google next week. Texas says the lab will involve up to 40 student researchers in its first year, scaling to 200 a year. Del Conte said the lab's construction should be finished in about three months. Goldsberry said it will be fully operational in 2027.

"I got undergrads who are dying to do it," Goldsberry said. "I got grad students who are already good at it. I got faculty who are teaching it. And then I got a lab full of athletes and teams and coaches that are desperate for it."

Texas uses a tool called Football Scouting Intelligence. It automates the opponent data and video reports that Sarkisian's staff used to compile by hand each week, Goldsberry said. The AI can also digest data from human movement tools developed by companies like Catapult, which track players' acceleration, deceleration, heart rate, and wear and tear. The lab plans to pull data into the system, starting with football.
Del Conte, who once picked up game tape at the bus station and spliced it for coaches, believes data will challenge play-calling habits in the near future.

You think your favorite play is the correct one to call in a certain situation? Well, Google Gemini might sort through the data and discover it's one of your least productive plays in that situation. "If it's someone's favorite play, you go, well, sir, that's the proof of the pudding," Del Conte said. "I don't think that's your favorite play anymore."

Football is part of the institute's longest-running projects with Texas athletics, but it has also helped scout players in the basketball transfer portal. Transfer AI grades players and projects how they would perform at Texas against an SEC schedule. Goldsberry said he brought in data scientists from his days with the Spurs to build models that rate roughly 5,000 men's and 5,000 women's college basketball players. Men's coach Sean Miller and women's coach Vic Schaefer use it, he said.
A football version generates scores for transfer targets at nearly every position group, according to the institute's website.
"I don't care if you're playing at Harvard, if you're playing at Michigan, if you're playing at Bowling Green, I've got you scouted," Goldsberry said.

The data also helps inform what Texas should pay players in revenue-sharing money. Goldsberry said finding the best player is no longer the whole problem; rather, "it's being the best player within our budget."

AI isn't new to football. NFL teams use Microsoft Copilot-powered tools in the coaching booth. In college, Arizona State's football program began using Intel AI-powered computers for recruiting and game preparation in 2025. Texas' pitch is scale: a university lab, Google engineers and student researchers building tools for 21 teams and more than 500 players.

The announcement Friday is big on ambition. Del Conte contends the Bevo Lab "will become the global benchmark for innovation in sports AI and data analytics." All 21 sports at the university will work with Bevo Lab.

Matt Renner, Google Cloud's president and chief revenue officer, is a Texas graduate who ran Microsoft's U.S. enterprise business before joining Google. The belief is other schools will want the same setup as Texas after it is fully up and running.
Google works with other universities, he said, but not at this level. "We're not leaning in like this," Renner said.
Del Conte said he hopes the model "spreads like wildfire" to other schools.

articles.headline: EXCLUSIVE: Fed timeline challenges reports of migrant baby facing immigration judge alone
keyFacts: Office of Refugee Resettlement officials said federal records show a 1-year-old migrant boy was not left without counsel due to systemic gaps.
